headline: Dry weather holds through Saturday, then forecasters are now more confident a coastal storm will bring a soaking rain and some wind to New York City and the region Sunday night into Monday, with a low-end flooding risk.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: High pressure keeps Friday and Friday night dry and quiet around New York City. Some shallow fog may form early Friday morning in outlying spots such as central Long Island, locally thick enough to cut visibility sharply. Winds stay light from the west-southwest Friday, turning light north-northwest Friday night, with some outlying areas going nearly calm.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: Saturday stays dry under high pressure. Rain chances develop on Sunday as a coastal low approaches, and the storm is now expected to pass through or just east of the New York area Sunday night into Monday. The air with this storm is very moist for November, but the low is forecast to move north fairly quickly, around 20 knots (about 23 mph), which should limit how long the heaviest rain lasts. The region is under a marginal (low-end) risk of rain heavy enough to cause flooding, and flooding potential late Sunday into Monday has been added to the Weather Service's hazardous weather outlook.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: Rain is likely early Monday, with improvement possible Monday afternoon and northwest winds gusting around 20–25 knots (roughly 25–30 mph); the latest models trend slightly lower on both rain amounts and wind because the storm looks weaker. Tuesday turns dry with weakening northwest winds. Another coastal storm is possible around Thanksgiving (Thursday), with about a 60 percent chance of precipitation, mostly rain, though some mixed precipitation is possible inland at the start; models disagree sharply on its track, from over Cape Cod to well south of the area, so uncertainty is very high.

coast: Winds and seas stay below Small Craft Advisory levels through Saturday. Seas build Sunday into Monday as the low approaches, possibly reaching 5 feet or more on the ocean by late Sunday, with small craft advisory or gale-force winds possible on all waters Monday depending on the storm's track and strength. Northwest winds behind the storm will likely reach Small Craft Advisory levels on Tuesday, especially on the ocean. A track along the coast would push water onshore ahead of Tuesday's full moon, but weaker winds may offset that; coastal flood guidance shows mostly a non-event, with minor flooding possible in the most vulnerable back-bay spots, and only the most extreme scenario brings Freeport to moderate flooding.
watch_for: The exact track and strength of the Sunday night–Monday storm, which could still nudge rain, wind and coastal flooding up or down.
Possible flooding from heavy rain late Sunday into Monday in flood-prone spots.
A second, highly uncertain coastal storm around Thanksgiving.
confidence: Confidence is high for dry weather through Saturday, increased (after models came together overnight) for a rainstorm Sunday night into Monday though details may still shift, and very low for the Thanksgiving storm.
